content: Children's Memorial Hospital employs nearly 1,100 pediatric specialists who focus on 70 different specialties across multiple locations. This hospital provides care to more children than any other hospital or medical center in the Chicago area. It is accredited by the Joint Commission, previously known as the Joint Commission on Accreditation of Healthcare Organizations. The hospital is licensed for 270 beds and specializes in treating critically ill children. Its Case Mix Index, a measure of patient severity, ranks it among the top five children's hospitals in the United States for consistently caring for severely ill pediatric patients. Children's Memorial Hospital was established in 1882 by Julia Foster Porter as the Maurice Porter Memorial Hospital. It began as an 8-bed facility located at the corner of Halsted and Belden streets in Chicago. It was the first hospital in Chicago dedicated exclusively to the care of children and the field of pediatrics. As the primary pediatric teaching hospital for Northwestern University's Feinberg School of Medicine, Children's Memorial Hospital offers one of the most competitive and sought-after pediatric residency programs in the country. The hospital is also home to the Children's Memorial Research Center, which serves as the research arm of the hospital and a virtual hub for pediatric research at Northwestern University's Feinberg School of Medicine. Founded in 1989, the research center has grown to include over 200 investigators and secures more than $25 million in external research funding, with two-thirds of this funding coming from the National Institutes of Health (NIH) and other federal agencies. The hospital's nursing department has received the prestigious Magnet Award for Nursing Excellence. Additionally, Children's Memorial has been recognized as one of the 25 best places to work by Chicago Magazine and one of the top 100 companies by Working Mother Magazine. Construction for a new facility is scheduled to begin in 2008 at the hospital's future site in the Streeterville area of Chicago, adjacent to the McGaw Medical Center of Northwestern University. The new 1-million-square-foot facility will feature 275 private rooms, with the capacity to expand to 343 rooms by 2017. On September 5, 2007, Chicago philanthropist Ann Lurie announced a record-breaking $100 million donation toward the new hospital. Upon completion, the new facility will be renamed the Ann & Robert H. Lurie Children's Hospital of Chicago. It will remain the only independent pediatric hospital in Illinois while continuing to strengthen its partnerships with Northwestern Memorial HealthCare and the Feinberg School of Medicine.
